title: A Blue Congress, Mr. Veto And A Treasury Twist
text:
A Blue Congress, Mr. Veto And A Treasury Twist

Will Denyer

Gavekal Research | 4 Nov 2026

The Democratic Party won majority control of both chambers of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections. However, the White House remains under Republican control, and the Democrats lack the two-thirds majority in both chambers of Congress required to override the presidential veto. Donald Trump has already promised to become “Mr. Veto.”The result will be legislative gridlock in 2027 and 2028. But first, markets need to navigate whatever the Republicans can achieve in the lame duck session, and even after that there are areas of policy—including foreign policy and Treasury financing—that can change without new legislation.
